title: Willpower Is Always on Will-Call
coreMove: Schedule the most important work for the part of the day when restraint and freshness are actually available.
sourcePressure: This lie chapter rejects the idea that willpower is always available and teaches the reader to place high-value work where energy and freshness are strongest.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating willpower as a personality trait or making claims about biology the source does not support.

hook: A single choice changes the whole day
The real priority is hiding under the busy work
Willpower Is Always on Will-Call as a generic focus opener
counterintuition: Focus is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: Set a timer and list priorities
Write down your one thing without a concrete context
examples: generic office worker choosing email or strategy
